description:
FILED s411 (Fable) while running Phase A4 (docs/plan-one-compiler-s411.md): making ExprToCL's decline sites DIE (rule 12) turned a silently-broken emission into an announced drop.

REPRO (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL):
  my @x=(1,2); sub f { my $s = "$_[$_[1]]"; print "$s\n" } f(7,0);   # perl 7
  my $y = "$x[$x[0]]"; print "$y\n";                                # perl 2
  PCL: `PCL: statement dropped â¦ PCL internal: no form emitter for expression leaf PPI::Token::Number:?` for both (before A4: the text emitter printed the empty leaf as `(p-aref @_ )` and SBCL died with simple-program-error at run time).

CAUSE: Pl/PExpr/StringInterpolation.pm's parse_array_subscript / parse_interpolated_variable â the hand-rolled subscript scanner (dup-census family 1) builds the INNER `$_[1]` index as a PPI::Token::Number with undef content.  Corpus: perl-tests/postfixderef.t line 353 (`bless [ "$_[$_[2]]"." plus "."$_[!$_[2]]" ]`, an overload sub) â added to docs/parse-error-drop-census-s399.tsv under the s409 census-INCREASE rule (crash-form â counted drop).

FIX: this is InterpScan consumer 3 territory (task #388, docs/interp-scan.md step 3: replace the low-level scanning with scan_one events) â a nested subscript is one of the divergences the port closes.  If the port slips, the local fix is in parse_array_subscript's recursion for a subscript whose index is itself a subscripted variable.  Guard row: a Pl/t transpile-test row with the two shapes above (perl oracle).
CLOSED s421 (Fable review): fixed by #414 (s420, the hollow-token anchor) —
verified by probe: `"$x[$b[1]]"` → 20, `sub f { "$_[$_[1]]" } f(7,0)` → 7,
and the ten-shape nested-subscript set identical to perl.  The DEREF sibling
(`"$$r[$i[1]]"`, `"${$r}[...]"`) is NOT covered — that is #420.
subject: "$a[$b[1]]" â a NESTED array subscript inside a dq string loses its inner index (StringInterpolation emits a content-less Number token): perl prints the element, PCL used to CRASH at run time on `(p-aref @_ )` and since s411 A4 DROPS the statement, announced
